evidence.content:
The repo rate is the interest rate at which the Reserve Bank of India lends short-term money to commercial banks against government securities, and it is the main tool of India's monetary policy.
 As of 13 October 2026, the repo rate is 5.50%. The RBI's Monetary Policy Committee raised it by 25 basis points on 7 October 2026 and shifted its stance to calibrated tightening. [...] As of 13 October 2026, the repo rate is 5.50%. According to the RBI’s press release, the Monetary Policy Committee voted unanimously on 7 October 2026 to raise the policy repo rate by 25 basis points to 5.50%. It also changed the stance to “calibrated tightening”, which signals that rate cuts are off the table in the near term and that the next move can only be a hike or a pause. This was the first hike since February 2023.

### RBI Policy Rates After the October 2026 Decision [...] ## Conclusion

The repo rate is the RBI’s main lever for steering inflation and growth. It currently stands at 5.50% after the October 2026 hike, it is set by the Monetary Policy Committee rather than by a formula, and it influences everything from bank borrowing costs to your home loan EMI. The reverse repo rate is its mirror image, and today the SDF rate does most of that work.

evidence.content:
### When did the UK standard VAT rate change to 20%?

  

The UK standard VAT rate rose to 20% on 4 January 2011, up from 17.5%. Before that, the rate was temporarily reduced to 15% from 1 December 2008 to 31 December 2009 as an economic stimulus during the financial crisis. Since January 2011 the rate has remained at 20%. When a rate change takes effect, businesses must apply the new rate from the date of change and may need to adjust prices, contracts and accounting systems. [...] The UK has three VAT rates. The standard rate is 20%, charged on most goods and services. The reduced rate is 5%, applied to specific items such as domestic energy, children's car seats and mobility aids for people aged 60 or over. The zero rate is 0%, covering most food, children's clothing and footwear, books and newspapers, women's sanitary products and public transport. Some supplies are exempt from VAT entirely, meaning no VAT is charged and input VAT cannot be reclaimed. [...] The UK standard VAT rate is 20% and applies to most goods and services unless HMRC specifically classifies them under a lower rate or as exempt.
 Reduced-rate items taxed at 5% include domestic fuel and power, children's car seats, smoking cessation products and mobility aids installed in the home of someone aged 60 or over. Women's sanitary products have been zero-rated since 1 January 2021, and energy-saving materials installed in homes are zero-rated until 31 March 2027.

evidence.content:
This guide walks through what the GST Act actually requires, the two tests you have to pass before you can zero-rate, the documentation IRAS expects you to keep, and the audit triggers we see most often.

## The basic rule (and where it stops being simple)

Singapore's GST rate is 9% (raised from 8% on 1 January 2024). If you're a GST-registered Singapore business, you charge 9% GST on most supplies of goods and services made in Singapore. [...] My customer is an overseas company that's also GST-registered in Singapore. What now? Read the contract carefully. If the contract is with the overseas head office, you can zero-rate (subject to the usual tests). If the contract is with their Singapore branch or subsidiary, you charge 9%, even though they can claim that GST back on their own return. Don't conflate the two scenarios. [...] In practice this means: rather than the overseas supplier charging you GST (which they typically can't, not being Singapore GST-registered), you self-account for the 9% GST on your inbound supply, recording it as both output and input tax in your GST return. For most fully-recovering businesses, the net effect is zero, but the reporting still has to happen.

evidence.title: Transitional Rules for GST Rate Change
evidence.content:
An overseas supplier that is GST registered under the OVR regime enters into a contract in Aug 2023 to provide remote services to a non-registered person in Singapore as follows:

Value of supply performed in 2023: $200 (4 x $50)

Value of supply performed on/ after 1 Jan 2024: $800 (16 x $50)

Based on the time of supply rules, GST is chargeable as follows:

 8% on payment of $100 received on 1 Sep 2023; and
 9% on $900 when invoice issued/balance payment received on 10 Jan 2024 [...] You procured imported services from your overseas supplier who performed the services on 21 Dec 2023 when the GST rate was 8%. The supplier’s invoice was issued on 11 Jan 2024 and you made the full payment on 23 Jan 2024.

Under the general time of supply rule, the supply of imported services is subject to reverse charge at 9% GST as the invoice was issued and full payment was made after the rate change. [...] You delivered goods to your customer on 26 Dec 2023 when the GST rate was 8%. You issued a tax invoice dated 3 Jan 2024 for the sales of goods and you received full payment from your customer on 10 Jan 2024.

Under the general time of supply rule, 9% GST is chargeable on the supply as the tax invoice is issued and full payment is received after the rate change. However, you can elect to charge 8% GST on the entire value of the supply as the goods were fully delivered in 2023.

evidence.title: EU AI Act High-Risk Deadline: Enterprise Readiness Gap – Lab Space
evidence.content:
August 2, 2026 is the binding enforcement date for high-risk AI system obligations under the EU AI Act, covering Articles 9–17 (provider requirements) and Article 26 (deployer requirements). Despite a November 2025 European Commission proposal to delay certain deadlines to late 2027, this extension has not been enacted into law and enterprises should treat August 2026 as the operative deadline. [...] ## Key Takeaways

The EU AI Act’s high-risk AI obligations represent the most operationally demanding wave of the regulation’s phased implementation. With the binding enforcement date approaching in August 2026 and compliance programs still nascent at many enterprises, organizations operating AI systems in regulated sectors face a narrow and compressing window to act. The following points summarize the most critical dimensions of this situation. [...] ## Background

The EU Artificial Intelligence Act (Regulation 2024/1689) entered into force on August 1, 2024, widely described as establishing the world’s first comprehensive horizontal legal framework for AI systems. The regulation takes a tiered approach, with obligations scaling to the assessed risk level of each system. The most consequential tier for the majority of enterprises—obligations applicable to high-risk AI systems under Annex III—become enforceable on August 2, 2026 .

evidence.title: UK Contactless Card Limit to be Abolished in March 2026 | Gary Prince posted on the topic | LinkedIn
evidence.content:

evidence.title: How the election of the Federal Chancellor works | Federal Chancellor
evidence.content:
The process for electing the Federal Chancellor is set out in Article 63 of the Basic Law (Grundgesetz). It provides that the Chancellor be elected by the Bundestag without debate on the proposal of the Federal President. The members of the Bundestag elect the Federal Chancellor on behalf of the voters.

Every four years, German citizens elect their representatives in the German Bundestag. The Bundestag then decides who should lead the Federal Government. [...] To become Federal Chancellor, a person must be at least 18 years of age and a German citizen. Holding a seat in the Bundestag is not a prerequisite. After consulting with each of the parliamentary groups in the Bundestag, the Federal President will propose a candidate for the office of Federal Chancellor.

## The election process [...] Where the Chancellor-elect secures an absolute majority, that is the votes of the majority of the Members of the Bundestag, the Federal President must appoint the Chancellor within seven days of the election. If the Chancellor-elect receives only a relative majority, i.e. the most votes, the Federal President must either appoint the Chancellor within seven days or must dissolve the Bundestag (Article 63.4 of the Basic Law).

Title: The King of Norway for 35 years
# The King of Norway for 35 years. His Majesty King Harald V was the King of Norway from 17 January 1991 until his death on 28 August 2026. Like his father and his grandfather, King Harald adopted the motto Alt for Norge (“We give our all for Norway”). King Harald was the third King of the modern Norwegian monarchy. With his gentle humour, strong sense of duty and impressive work capacity, he became a beloved monarch who was known for his compassion and ability to see the good in others. King Harald was deeply committed to Norway, and viewed himself as called to royal service. In addition to his constitutional duties as monarch – such as opening the Storting (Norwegian Parliament) each autumn, presiding over the Council of State and receiving ambassadors to Norway in a formal audience – King Harald met people all over the country during his many trips across Norway. King Harald was a focal point, unifying the country in times of joy as well as sorrow. The image of the Norwegian monarch and his family waving from the Palace Balcony has been the quintessential symbol of Constitution Day in Norway since 1905. As the King of this nation, I feel for each and every one of you.". And I firmly believe that we will uphold our ability to live freely and securely in our own country.". King Harald and Queen Sonja attached great importance to visiting all the counties across Norway and paid official visits to 353 of Norway’s 357 municipalities. King Harald and Queen Sonja also hosted a broad range of events at the Royal Palace to honour the efforts of volunteers, dedicated local leaders, athletes and others who in various ways had worked to benefit Norwegian society. During their 35 years as Norway’s King and Queen, he and Queen Sonja carried out 50 state visits abroad and hosted many international Heads of State while they were visiting Norway. He also attended the consecration of bishops and enjoyed paying visits to churches in cities and villages during his official trips in Norway, as well as to the Sjømannskirken – Norwegian Church Abroad – when he was in other countries.

Norway has a long tradition of close ties between the Head of State and the Armed Forces. The monarch is always accompanied by an aide-de-camp from one of the branches of the military, and conducts regular audiences with the Chief of Defence and the heads of various Armed Forces departments. On a number of occasions, he was the one who awarded the War Cross, Norway's highest decoration. King Harald was part of a long line of tradition extending back to King Haakon VII – and forward to King Haakon VIII and Crown Princess Ingrid Alexandra. King Olav V was trained at the Royal Norwegian Military Academy, and served among other things as Chief of Defence during parts of World War II. The cleanest option, and the right long-term answer for most teams, is upgrading to a supported Django release. Right now, that means either Django 5.2 LTS – supported until April 2028 – or the latest version, Django 6.0, which runs until April 2027.

That’s the easy part to say. The harder part is that for many production applications, especially ones that have been running on 3.2 or 4.2 for years, an upgrade isn’t a weekend task. [...] Pro Tip: The last feature release of a major version will be an LTS release. Always anchor your Django version choice to an LTS release. The three-year window gives you actual breathing room for planned upgrades.

Here is the current status of recent Django project versions:

## Risks of Django EOL for Your Organization [...] ## Django Release Cycle and End of Life Timeline

Django follows a predictable release date cadence – a feature release happens every eight months approximately. Each release goes through two security support phases before it’s retired at the end.

Standard Releases (Non-LTS) get eight months of active support, followed by another eight months of security-only support. Sixteen months total. After that, they reach EOL.

Microsoft on March 23 released TypeScript 6.0, the final major version built on the project's original JavaScript compiler codebase. evidence.content:
The 2026 Social Security wage base is $184,500, the maximum amount of earnings subject to the 6.2% Social Security (OASDI) payroll tax in 2026, up from $176,100 in 2025 (Source: SSA, “Contribution and Benefit Base,” ssa.gov/oact/cola/cbb.html). Earning at or above the wage base is one requirement for the maximum Social Security benefit in 2026.

Table of Contents

Toggle

Last reviewed: October 5, 2026 | Written and reviewed by Craig Wear, CFP®, founder of Q3 Advisors [...] The Social Security wage base for 2026 is $184,500. This is the maximum amount of annual earnings on which the 6.2% Social Security (OASDI) payroll tax is charged. Any wages above $184,500 in 2026 are exempt from the Social Security portion of FICA tax (Source: SSA, “Contribution and Benefit Base,” ssa.gov/oact/cola/cbb.html). The wage base is separate from the Social Security earnings test for 2026.

## Talk With Craig Wear's Team [...] Contact Us today

The formal name for this figure is the “contribution and benefit base,” also called the taxable maximum. The Social Security Administration adjusts it each year based on the national average wage index (Source: SSA, “Contribution and Benefit Base Determination,” ssa.gov/oact/cola/cbbdet.html). The $184,500 cap applies only to Social Security tax: the 1.45% Medicare (Hospital Insurance) tax has no wage cap and applies to all earnings in 2026.

The federal minimum wage, established by the Fair Labor Standards Act (FLSA), is currently $7.25 per hour. The U.S. federal government establishes the base federal minimum wage, outlines regulations for overtime compensation, and stipulates conditions for hiring young workers. This law defines the foundational standards that all states must meet or exceed. [...] What happens if a state minimum wage is lower than the federal rate?  
 The federal rate of $7.25 applies. Georgia and Wyoming have state laws below the federal minimum, but employers in those states still owe $7.25 per hour under the FLSA.

How do I handle minimum wage for remote workers in high-wage cities?  
 You owe the local minimum for hours worked within that jurisdiction, regardless of where your company is based.

evidence.title: Energy Bills Price Cap 2026: Current Ofgem Rates Explained - BLUETTI UK
evidence.content:
As of 8 September 2026, the current Ofgem cap period runs from 1 July to 30 September 2026. For a typical dual-fuel household paying by Direct Debit, the headline annualised figure is £1,663. The average electricity rate is 26.11p/kWh, with a 57.19p/day standing charge, while gas costs 7.33p/kWh with a 29.04p/day standing charge. [...] The next cap period runs from 1 October to 31 December 2026. The headline figure rises by 4% to £1,723 for typical Direct Debit dual-fuel consumption. Average electricity rates will be 26.32p/kWh with a 54.83p/day standing charge, while gas will be 7.97p/kWh with a 29.68p/day standing charge. Actual rates vary by region and payment method.

## What Does the Energy Price Cap Actually Limit? [...] The Ofgem energy price cap limits unit rates and standing charges for standard variable tariffs in Great Britain; it does not set a maximum total bill. From 1 July to 30 September 2026, the typical Direct Debit dual-fuel headline figure is £1,663 a year. From 1 October, it rises by 4% to £1,723.

evidence.title: Energy price cap will rise by 4% from October 2026 | Ofgem
evidence.content:
The current price cap for a typical household paying by direct debit for gas and electricity is £1,663. Based on the energy use of a typical domestic household, from October, the price cap will rise by £60 per year (or £5 per month) to £1,723 for the average household using both electricity and gas if this level was sustained for a year. Around 35% of households are on fixed tariffs and will not be affected by this rise- this is about 11 million households. [...] Under the updated TDCV, the typical household bill from October will rise from its current figure of £1,663 per year to £1,723. For reference, if calculated against the old TDCV rate (2023) this number would have been £1,862 rising to £1,935 from October.  
   TDCV is a presentational tool, but updating it impacts the cap unit rate because suppliers will need to recover certain costs over fewer units of demand.

evidence.title: How long is a Go version supported? The two release rule
evidence.content:
3 min read

A Go major release is supported until two newer major releases are out, which works out to about a year. With Go 1.27 released on 19 August 2026, Go 1.26 and 1.27 are the supported lines. Go 1.25 has dropped out of support.

## The rule [...] | Major | Initial release | Last patch listed | Date of that patch | Supported? |
 ---  --- 
| 1.27 | 2026-08-19 | 1.27.2 | 2026-10-08 | Yes |
| 1.26 | 2026-02-10 | 1.26.9 | 2026-10-08 | Yes |
| 1.25 | 2025-08-12 | 1.25.14 | 2026-08-19 | No, ended with 1.27 |
| 1.24 | 2025-02-11 | 1.24.13 | 2026-02-04 | No |

The last row shows how it looks in practice. The final patch for a line lands when the second newer major ships, and then the line goes quiet.

## What the security fixes cover [...] No. Under the two newer releases rule, it ended when Go 1.27 shipped.

 Do I need to upgrade Go to get a standard library fix?

You need to rebuild with a toolchain that contains the fix. That usually means a patch revision of a supported major.
